sources.title: Capturing Delayed Feedback in Conversion Rate Prediction via Elapsed-Time Sampling
sources.accessLimitation: The method and experiments concern conversion-rate prediction; only the delayed-observation problem and freshness-versus-label-completeness trade-off transfer generally.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck only if the publisher record changes or is withdrawn; method applicability must be re-evaluated per workload.
sources.supports: Original evidence that outcomes arriving after prediction can create inaccurate temporary labels.
sources.limitations: Does not establish that its estimator or reported performance transfers outside the studied conversion setting.

sources.title: Datasheets for Datasets
sources.accessLimitation: The stable arXiv identity exposes revision history; the proposal is documentation guidance, not a data-quality certification.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck at publication freezes for arXiv continuity and preserve the exact revision used during canonical integration.
sources.supports: Dataset motivation, composition, collection, recommended use, distribution, and maintenance should travel from creator to consumer.
sources.limitations: A datasheet records assertions and questions; it does not execute validation or settle legal authority.

sources.title: Data Cards: Purposeful and Transparent Dataset Documentation for Responsible AI
sources.accessLimitation: A documentation framework evaluated through bounded case studies; documentation does not itself validate data quality or permission.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck at publication freezes for index continuity; retain the 2022 paper identity.
sources.supports: Dataset origins, development, intent, collection, annotation, evolution, and decisions should be documented for lifecycle stakeholders.
sources.limitations: Does not prescribe executable schema checks, retention law, or domain label validity.

sources.title: Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work: Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI
sources.accessLimitation: Interview study of 53 practitioners in bounded high-stakes contexts; the reported 92 percent prevalence is sample-specific and must not be generalized.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck at publication freezes for paper access; keep empirical claims tied to the study sample and methods.
sources.supports: Early, distributed data-definition and documentation failures can compound downstream and cross organizational boundaries.
sources.limitations: Does not establish universal causal frequency, a technical validator, or authority transfer to the MLE.

sources.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
sources.authorOrg: Google Research and the paper authors
sources.accessLimitation: The paper is a durable 2015 conceptual and systems analysis; named mechanisms and organization examples are not current product prescriptions, and its failure taxonomy is not a prevalence estimate for every organization.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck at blueprint, manuscript, and publication freeze for page and final-paper availability; pair every contemporary mechanism with current official documentation.
sources.supports: ML systems can accumulate system-level debt through data dependencies, undeclared consumers, feedback loops, entanglement, pipeline coupling, and configuration interactions.
sources.limitations: The taxonomy diagnoses transferable failure mechanisms but does not assign formal authority, provide a current control catalog, quantify a particular workload's debt, or prove that a given workload exhibits those failures.

sources.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
sources.authorOrg: Google Research and the paper authors
sources.accessLimitation: The first-party research index exposes final publication metadata and the proposal's reporting categories; it is not a mandatory standard or proof that documentation makes a model suitable.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck the Google Research record and final-paper link at blueprint, manuscript, and publication freeze while preserving the 2019 paper identity.
sources.supports: A model report can preserve intended and excluded uses, evaluation procedures and data, relevant conditions and subgroup factors, metrics, ethical considerations, caveats, limitations, and recommendations.
sources.limitations: A model card is a reporting structure, not proof of accuracy, fairness, safety, compliance, qualification, release approval, or an authority to set acceptance thresholds.

sources.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction
sources.authorOrg: Google Research and the paper authors
sources.accessLimitation: The 28-test rubric reflects the authors' production experience; it is a dated method and diagnostic vocabulary, not a certification, universal gate, current platform policy, or audited outcome.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck at publication freezes for record and final-paper availability; translate its tests into current workload evidence rather than copying a score threshold.
sources.supports: Production readiness requires explicit data, feature, model, infrastructure, and monitoring tests beyond offline model quality, with test categories selected and interpreted in context.
sources.limitations: The rubric does not establish universal pass scores, domain acceptance, safety, privacy, security, compliance, business outcomes, or workload-specific authority.

sources.title: The Tail at Scale
sources.accessLimitation: The examples concern large distributed online services; transfer to an ML workload requires representative workload-specific traces and no fleet-scale extrapolation.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck only if the publication page or linked paper becomes unavailable; doctrine is durable.
sources.supports: Tail latency can dominate whole-service responsiveness and must be measured as a distribution under load.
sources.limitations: Does not specify ML-specific model quality, current accelerator capacity, or a universal percentile/SLO threshold.

sources.title: Improving Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research: A Report from the NeurIPS 2019 Reproducibility Program
sources.authorOrg: Pineau et al.; Journal of Machine Learning Research
sources.accessLimitation: Research-program evidence concerns published ML research and must be transferred cautiously to production run reconstruction.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck URL at publication freeze; re-evaluate transfer language if newer consensus terminology changes the reproducibility taxonomy.
sources.supports: Reproducibility depends on inspectable code, data, reporting, and workflow artifacts rather than a seed alone. Reproducibility programs improve the ability to examine reliability but do not erase environmental bounds.
sources.limitations: Does not specify a production manifest schema or promise bitwise identity across hardware.

sources.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
sources.authorOrg: Cawley and Talbot; Journal of Machine Learning Research
sources.accessLimitation: Empirical results use specific benchmark settings; the general selection-bias mechanism is the durable support.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck URL at publication freeze; retain limitations if later methods are substituted.
sources.supports: Optimizing a finite-sample selection criterion can overfit that criterion and bias subsequent performance estimates. Model selection should be treated as part of fitting and repeated independently inside evaluation trials.
sources.limitations: Does not identify a universally best validation design or authorize release.

sources.title: Gender Shades: Intersectional Accuracy Disparities in Commercial Gender Classification
sources.authorOrg: Buolamwini and Gebru; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research
sources.accessLimitation: The audit covers three 2017-era commercial gender-classification systems and a specific phenotypic/demographic dataset; it is not a current vendor ranking or a universal fairness result.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck URL at publication freeze and preserve the historical evaluation date, task, systems, groups, and dataset boundaries.
sources.supports: The authors constructed a gender- and skin-type-balanced evaluation set and reported large intersectional error disparities across three commercial systems. The maximum reported error for darker-skinned women was 34.7%, while the maximum for lighter-skinned men was 0.8%.
sources.limitations: Supports the need to inspect meaningful intersections; it cannot define appropriate groups or thresholds for another workload.

sources.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
sources.authorOrg: Guo, Pleiss, Sun, and Weinberger; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research
sources.accessLimitation: Experiments concern selected image/document classifiers and architectures; temperature scaling is not universally sufficient.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck URL at publication freeze and keep dataset/model/method bounds visible in any worked example.
sources.supports: Calibration asks whether predicted confidence corresponds to observed correctness likelihood. The authors found selected modern neural networks miscalibrated and reported temperature scaling effective on most evaluated datasets.
sources.limitations: Accuracy and calibration are distinct; calibration results do not establish downstream safety, domain validity, or segment sufficiency.

sources.title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
sources.authorOrg: Original paper authors; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research
sources.accessLimitation: Benchmark evidence spans selected datasets and specified shift types; it does not represent every deployment population or consequence.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck PMLR record at publication freezes; preserve the 2021 benchmark scope and avoid importing benchmark visuals.
sources.supports: Training and test distributions can differ materially in real-world settings and evaluation should preserve named shift contexts.
sources.limitations: Benchmark performance cannot authorize real-world use or set a workload's split strategy.

sources.title: Leakage in Data Mining: Formulation, Detection, and Avoidance
sources.authorOrg: Tel Aviv University record for original paper authors
sources.accessLimitation: The institutional record exposes metadata and abstract; full publisher access may require ACM access. The methodology is general and thresholds remain workload-specific.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck institutional record and DOI at publication freezes; replace only with an author-controlled full-text record if the current page is withdrawn.
sources.supports: Leakage can be framed as target information illegitimately available to modeling, and learn-predict separation provides a general avoidance method.
sources.limitations: The paper does not enumerate every modern leakage mode or prove a particular split valid.

sources.title: Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering
sources.accessLimitation: First-party practice guidance derived from Google systems; its numbered rules and examples are contextual, not universal doctrine.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck the living page at all three publication freezes and record material rule-number or content changes.
sources.supports: Start with a simple incumbent, measure before optimizing, retain end-to-end pipeline integrity, and measure train-serving skew.
sources.limitations: Named Google mechanisms and observations require transfer tests; the guide does not decide intended purpose or acceptable consequence.

sources.title: Reproducibility
sources.accessLimitation: PyTorch 2.13 documentation is framework-, release-, platform-, and hardware-specific. It explicitly states that complete reproducibility is not guaranteed across releases, commits, platforms, or CPU/GPU execution and that deterministic operations can carry performance and coverage tradeoffs.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck the pinned 2.13 page at every freeze and whenever the recorded PyTorch, CUDA, cuDNN, platform, hardware, or deterministic-operation context changes; never return to the mutable stable URL for this identity.
sources.supports: Seeded randomness and deterministic algorithms can bound repeatability within a recorded context, while exact cross-release or cross-platform reproducibility remains unsupported.
sources.limitations: PyTorch controls do not cover every external source of nondeterminism, prove that a workload is reproducible, or establish how another framework or service behaves.

sources.title: Nested versus non-nested cross-validation
sources.accessLimitation: The worked example uses Iris and current scikit-learn APIs; it illustrates rather than universally quantifies selection bias.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck at every freeze and pin a version if code or screenshots are planned.
sources.supports: Non-nested reuse of data for tuning and evaluation can yield an optimistic score. Nested evaluation separates hyperparameter selection from generalization estimation.
sources.limitations: A nested split is not automatically representative, uncertainty-complete, or appropriate for every data structure.

sources.title: Probability calibration
sources.accessLimitation: Current library behavior and API; examples do not prove a selected calibration method generalizes to the target population.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck at every freeze and pin a version before any executable blueprint or numeric example.
sources.supports: Reliability diagrams compare binned predicted probabilities with observed positive-class frequencies. Cross-validated calibration helps keep calibration fitting separate from base-estimator fitting.
sources.limitations: Binning, sample size, split design, scoring, and model/output type constrain interpretation.

sources.title: TensorFlow Data Validation
sources.accessLimitation: The living framework tutorial demonstrates schema, anomaly, categorical drift, and train/evaluation/serving skew mechanisms with example comparators and thresholds; it does not determine semantic validity, acceptable shift, or outcome degradation.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck at every freeze and whenever TFX/TFDV releases alter schemas, comparators, API fields, threshold behavior, or tutorial semantics.
sources.supports: Executable schema and anomaly checks plus train, evaluation, serving, and prior-span comparisons can expose schema, feature, distribution, drift, and skew evidence; threshold selection remains explicit.
sources.limitations: Detection coverage and thresholds are implementation- and domain-specific. Passing input comparisons does not prove provenance, permission, representativeness, label truth, model adequacy, causal attribution, or permission to retrain and promote.

sources.title: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles
sources.authorOrg: International Medical Device Regulators Forum; U.S. Food and Drug Administration publication page
sources.accessLimitation: The FDA page identifies and links the final IMDRF N88 technical document; the principles remain sector-specific and do not transfer formal device authorization or clinical validity to an MLE.
sources.recheckTrigger: Recheck the FDA/IMDRF publication status at each freeze and preserve the N88 FINAL:2025 edition identity if cited.
sources.supports: Study participants and datasets should represent the intended population and test sets should remain independent from training sets. Performance goals follow intended use, clinical risks, relevant conditions, local/global performance, and uncertainty.
sources.limitations: Transfer only the representative-evaluation and consequence principles; do not turn this book into medical-device guidance.
